headline: Qualcomm and Arm opened a jury trial in Delaware in which Qualcomm accuses Arm of withholding chip testing tools and seeks to stop paying royalties worth billions of dollars.
score_reason: Kept at the pool level: a major licensing fight between two big chip firms, though the claims are allegations and the outcome is not yet known.
importance_line: The result could change how much Qualcomm pays Arm for the chip designs behind its processors, but Qualcomm's claims are allegations that Arm denies, and the judge may narrow the damages.
summary: Reuters reports that Qualcomm, a major maker of chips for Android phones, and Arm Holdings, which supplies core chip-design technology to Qualcomm and others, began a five-day jury trial on 5 Oct 2026 in a US federal court in Delaware. Qualcomm accuses Arm of withholding chip testing tools it was owed and of leaking a 2024 threat to cancel their licence, which it says hurt its chip-deal talks with Meta Platforms, and seeks to stop paying royalties, potentially worth billions of dollars, for up to five years; Arm denies breaching the contract, and the judge is weighing whether to throw out that part of the contract, which could limit Qualcomm to smaller damages.
notes: Reuters page blocked (HTTP 401); wire text read in The Economic Times' copy and credited to Reuters, linked to the Reuters page. A related judge-only trial on whether Arm negotiated in good faith over its next chip technology is not covered in the summary.
